label: Population parameter
definition: A numerical feature of the population, such as its mean or the difference between treatment groups.

label: Sample estimate
definition: A value calculated from a sample to estimate a population quantity. Another sample may give a different value.

label: Difference observed in previous data
definition: The between-group difference calculated from an earlier sample. It can inform planning, with uncertainty; the chronic pain pilot showed a 40-percentage-point difference.

label: Target difference
definition: The between-group difference used to calculate the sample size at the chosen power. It can equal the difference observed in previous data or clinical threshold; the three roles have no fixed numerical order.

label: Clinical threshold
definition: The smallest between-group benefit judged worthwhile, considering risks, burden and alternatives.

label: Between-group differences and individual benefit
definition: A comparison of group averages or percentages. Individual patients may benefit by different amounts; the group comparison cannot identify how much each person would benefit.

label: Percentage points
definition: The absolute difference between two percentages: 60% minus 30% equals 30 percentage points.

label: Mean difference
definition: The difference between two group averages, in the outcome's original units. Here, novel treatment minus standard treatment.

label: Effect size
definition: A number describing the size of a difference or association, on a stated scale.

label: Standard deviation
definition: How much individual observations vary, measured in the outcome's units. Often abbreviated SD.

label: Standard error
definition: How much an estimate would vary across repeated samples. A smaller standard error means greater precision.

label: Confidence interval
definition: A range of values compatible with the data under the analysis assumptions. A narrower interval indicates greater precision at the same confidence level.

label: Estimation
definition: Using sample data to estimate a population quantity, such as a mean or a treatment difference.

label: Precision
definition: How little an estimate varies across repeated samples. At the same confidence level, a narrower confidence interval indicates greater precision.

label: Margin of error
definition: For a symmetric confidence interval, the distance from the estimate to either limit: half the full width.

label: Full interval width
definition: The upper confidence limit minus the lower limit. For a symmetric interval, it is twice the margin of error.

label: Null hypothesis
definition: The statement tested against the data. In these treatment comparisons, it says there is no population difference between treatments.

label: Alternative hypothesis
definition: In these two-sided comparisons, a population difference in either direction: the novel treatment could perform better or worse.

label: Type I error probability
definition: The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true: a false positive.

label: Type II error probability
definition: The probability of missing a specified true difference: a false negative.

label: Statistical power
definition: The probability that the planned test detects a specified true difference. It equals 1 minus the Type II error probability.

label: P-value
definition: Assuming the null hypothesis and model are correct, the probability of a test result at least as extreme as the one observed.

label: Two-sided test
definition: A test that allows evidence of a difference in either direction: the novel treatment could perform better or worse than the comparator.

label: Independent groups
definition: Separate groups of participants whose outcomes are assumed independent. Paired measurements or people grouped within clinics may need a different analysis.

label: Analyzable sample size
definition: The number of participants contributing to the planned analysis. Counts should specify whether they are per group or total.

label: Sampling variability
definition: The variation in results between samples from the same population. Larger independent samples generally reduce it.

label: Bias
definition: Systematic error that shifts an estimate away from the population value, for example when missing outcomes disproportionately come from patients with poor results.

label: Sensitivity analysis
definition: Checking how a result changes when you use other plausible assumptions, such as a smaller treatment difference or more missing outcomes.

label: Estimand
definition: The precise population quantity your study aims to estimate, including which treatments and outcome are compared and how treatment changes are handled.

label: Monte Carlo error
definition: Random variation caused by using a limited number of simulated studies. More simulation repetitions reduce this uncertainty.

label: False positive
definition: A statistically significant treatment difference when the population outcomes are equal: a Type I error.

label: False negative
definition: A non-significant finding despite a specified true population difference: a Type II error.

label: True positive
definition: A statistically significant finding when a population difference exists. Its probability at the specified true difference is power.

label: True negative
definition: A non-significant result when the null hypothesis is true.

label: Z-value
definition: A position on the standard normal bell-shaped curve, measured in standard deviations from its center.

label: Quantile
definition: A cutoff with a specified percentage of values below it. For example, 97.5% of the standard normal distribution lies below 1.96.

label: WMO
aliases: Medical Research Involving Human Subjects Act (WMO)
definition: The Medical Research Involving Human Subjects Act: Dutch legislation covering specified medical research involving people.

label: METC
aliases: medical research ethics committee (METC, or MREC in English)
definition: An accredited medical research ethics committee in the Netherlands. It reviews studies assigned to it under the applicable rules.

label: CCMO
definition: The Central Committee on Research Involving Human Subjects in the Netherlands. It oversees ethics review and directly reviews specified categories of research.

label: Research ethics committee
definition: An independent committee that reviews a study's scientific justification and protection of participants. Its name and responsibilities vary by country.

label: Institutional review board
definition: The usual US term for a committee that reviews research involving human participants.

label: Unit of randomization
definition: What is assigned to a treatment: for example, a participant, hospital, or body site.

label: Unit of measurement
definition: What each recorded outcome describes: for example, a participant, lesion, or visit.

label: Unit of analysis
definition: What the analysis treats as a unit. The method must account for relationships among measurements from the same participant or group.

label: Paired observations
definition: Two linked measurements, such as outcomes from two body sites in one participant. Their relationship is accounted for in a paired analysis.

label: Intracluster correlation coefficient (ICC)
definition: A measure of how similar outcomes are within the same group, such as patients within a hospital.

label: Design effect
definition: A factor describing how a study design changes the variance of an estimate compared with a design using independent observations.

label: Retention
definition: The percentage of enrolled participants who provide the required outcome at the specified time. If 180 of 200 contribute, retention is 90%.

label: Relative increase
definition: The increase divided by the starting value: from 80% to 96%, (96 - 80)/80 = 0.20, a 20% relative increase. The absolute increase is 16 percentage points.

label: Covariate adjustment
definition: Using characteristics measured before treatment, such as baseline pain, in the analysis. These can help improve precision.

label: Treatment crossover
definition: Receiving the other treatment after randomization. This can reduce the difference between randomized groups.

label: Treatment contamination
definition: Participants assigned to the comparator receive some or all of the intervention, potentially reducing the difference between randomized groups.

label: Primary outcome
definition: The main outcome chosen to answer the research question and guide the sample size calculation.

label: Pilot study
definition: A small preliminary study used to assess whether and how a larger study can be carried out.

label: Study protocol
definition: The written plan for a study, including its question, design, procedures and intended analysis.

label: Binary outcome
definition: An outcome with two possible categories, such as pain relief: yes or no.

label: PICO
definition: Population, Intervention, Comparator, and Outcome: four parts of a clear treatment-comparison question.

label: ICH E9
definition: Statistical guidance from the International Council for Harmonisation for planning, analyzing and reporting clinical trials of medicines.

label: SPIRIT
definition: Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials. Guidance on what to include in a trial protocol.

label: CONSORT
definition: Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials. Guidance on what to report about a randomized trial and its results.

label: STROBE
definition: Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology. Guidance for reporting observational studies.

label: STARD
definition: Standards for Reporting Diagnostic Accuracy Studies. Guidance for reporting studies of how well diagnostic tests work.

label: DELTA²
definition: Difference ELicitation in TriAls, second guidance project. Guidance on choosing and justifying the target difference for a sample size calculation.

label: Frequentist methods
definition: Statistical methods interpreted through their performance across hypothetical repetitions of the same study.

label: Statistical significance
definition: A result meeting the planned threshold for evidence against the null hypothesis.

label: Multiplicity
definition: Multiple opportunities for false-positive claims across a specified set of tests. The intended claims determine the appropriate error control.

label: Co-primary outcomes
definition: Primary outcomes whose required tests must all succeed to support the intended joint claim.

label: Interim analysis
definition: An analysis of accumulating trial results before the planned final analysis.

label: Futility
definition: A low prospect of demonstrating the planned benefit under a specified decision rule and assumptions.

label: Group-sequential design
definition: A trial with planned analyses and stopping opportunities, using a testing procedure that accounts for the repeated analyses.

label: Adaptive design
definition: A design allowing prespecified changes, such as revising sample size, in response to accumulating trial data.
